Question 11(c) [4 marks]: With reference to a business you have studied, explain how the use of an operations strategy has improved the performance objectives of cost and speed.
STIMULUS / CASE INFORMATION:
Snowy Ice-Creams Pty Ltd is opening a new store in the city. They plan on purchasing machinery to make all products on site. They will be selling 30 different flavours of ice-cream varieties as well as several cake desserts.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 4):
4 marks: Provides cause and effect in a case study addressing operations strategy to improve performance
3 marks: Provides characteristics and features in a case study addressing operations strategy to improve performance
2 marks: Provides theoretical cause and effect addressing operations strategy to improve performance
1 marks: Provides characteristics and features addressing operations strategy to improve performance

SAMPLE ANSWER (official):
Outsourcing is the contracting out of a non-core business activity. A business may wish to focus on its main activity, and so organises another business to provide a support service such as transport, supply chain management, producing components or supplying materials. By outsourcing, a business can free up resources to invest in core activities. Apple uses outsourcing effectively: by contracting the production of Apple products to Foxconn, Apple can focus on R&D and marketing, which Apple excels at. Apple can also achieve economies of scale through outsourcing, as large quantities of product are manufactured, driving down raw material costs through bulk buying and Foxconn running large production volumes.

ANSWERS COULD INCLUDE (the student does not need every point):
New product or service design and development; SCM (logistics, e-commerce, global sourcing); outsourcing; technology; inventory management; quality management.
